name: Pass Thurn
kurzbeschreibung: The Pass Thurn at 1,274 m elevation connects the Kitzbüheler Alpen with the Oberpinzgau and offers a spectacular view of the Wildkogel.
preis: Kostenlos frei zugänglich (Panoramabahn Berg- und Talfahrt ca. 24 €)
beschreibung:
Overview

The Pass Thurn crests at an elevation of 1,274 meters, linking the Tyrolean Leukental valley near Kitzbühel and Jochberg with the Upper Pinzgau region of Salzburg near Mittersill. Operating as an ancient alpine transit artery across the rolling slate ridges of the Kitzbühel Alps, the pass demarcates the provincial frontier between Tyrol and Salzburg. While renowned in winter as the northern portal to the expansive KitzSki arena, summer unveils a peaceful haven of biodiversity and panoramic beauty. Immediately adjacent to the pass summit unfolds the remarkable Wasenmoos: protected as a wetland sanctuary of European importance (Natura 2000), this primeval peat bog preserves rare carnivorous sundew flora, cranberry mosses, cotton grasses, and nesting grounds for black grouse. Engineered timber boardwalks and interactive interpretive trails guide visitors safely across the trembling peat, backdropped to the south by the glaciated peaks of Hohe Tauern National Park.

Route & Requirements

Trail options surrounding Pass Thurn excel in universal family access alongside rewarding alpine ridge traverses. The signature excursion is the Wasenmoos Moorland Nature Trail: level timber boardwalks and smooth gravel tracks guide visitors around fragile peat pools and up to a wooden panoramic viewing tower in about 45 to 60 minutes (distance approx. 2.5 km, easy grade T1, fully wheelchair and stroller accessible). Energetic mountain walkers utilize Pass Thurn as a springboard for ridge treks up toward the Resterhöhe (1,894 m) or the Zweitausender (2,004 m): the nearby Panoramabahn gondola ascends effortlessly to the crest, where walkers follow blooming alpine rose pastures to rustic dairies like the Toni-Alm or Pinzgauer Hütte (2 to 3 hours, moderate grade T1/T2). Comfortable walking shoes suffice for the moor; sturdy boots are advisable for ridge paths. Leashed dogs are welcome throughout the reserve.

Visit & Arrival

Rail passengers travel via ÖBB mainline trains into Kitzbühel or Mittersill stations. Connecting regional bus line 4010 services Pass Thurn regularly, stopping directly at "Pass Thurn Passhöhe" and "Wasenmoos". Motorists take the Inntal autobahn A12 (exit Wörgl-Ost), following highway B170 through Kitzbühel onto federal highway B161 directly over the pass. Generous free parking and national park info kiosks are located right at the summit. The Wasenmoos moorland trail is open year-round with free public access.

Tips

Climb the timber observation platform at the heart of Wasenmoos to photograph the dark peat tarns reflecting the snowy ice walls of the Großvenediger. Stop at the traditional Gasthof Pass Thurn or rustic Toni-Alm to enjoy piping-hot Pinzgau cheese dumplings served directly from a cast-iron skillet.
